english: The ten cards ace, $2,3,\dots,10$ of hearts are taken from a pack of playing cards, the ace being counted as $1$. Three of these ten cards are drawn at random, simultaneously. Then the probability that the sum of the numbers on the three cards drawn is divisible by $3$ is ______.
hindi: ताश की एक गड्डी से पान के दस पत्ते इक्का, $2,3,\dots,10$ लिए जाते हैं, जहाँ इक्के को $1$ गिना जाता है। इन दस पत्तों में से तीन पत्ते एक साथ यादृच्छया निकाले जाते हैं। तब निकाले गए तीनों पत्तों पर अंकित संख्याओं का योग $3$ से विभाज्य होने की प्रायिकता ______ है।
solution: Sum $\equiv0$ (mod $3$) iff all three remainders are equal or they are $0,1,2$
solution_full: All $\binom{10}{3}=120$ selections of three cards are equally likely.
Only the remainders on division by $3$ matter. Remainder $0$: $3,6,9$ ($3$ cards). Remainder $1$: $1,4,7,10$ ($4$ cards). Remainder $2$: $2,5,8$ ($3$ cards).

Three remainders $r_{1},r_{2},r_{3}\in\{0,1,2\}$ add to a multiple of $3$ exactly when they are all equal ($0+0+0$, $1+1+1$, $2+2+2$) or all different ($0+1+2$); two equal and one different never works.
Counts: all remainder $0$: $\binom{3}{3}=1$; all remainder $1$: $\binom{4}{3}=4$; all remainder $2$: $\binom{3}{3}=1$; one of each: $3\cdot4\cdot3=36$. Total $42$.
Probability $=\dfrac{42}{120}=\dfrac{7}{20}=0.35$. (The value $\dfrac{1}{3}$ would hold only if the three classes had equal sizes.)
originality_note: New: a card selection whose values split into unequal residue classes (3, 4, 3), so the familiar answer 1/3 fails and the count has to be done by classes (way 5: cards linked with combinations by residue classes). Closest known: 'three numbers from 1 to 3n, sum divisible by 3' and a 2007 contest problem on three of ten cards. Different because: the unequal classes change the answer and the combinations per class must be counted.
